say: Why do we have seasons? Most people guess it is our distance from the Sun.
But Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.
scenes.title: Why seasons?

say: The real reason is a tilt. Earth's axis leans about twenty-three and a half degrees,
and it keeps pointing the same way all year as we orbit.

manim.code:
class Orbit(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        orbit = Ellipse(width=10, height=4.6, color=GOLD, stroke_opacity=0.6)
        sun = Circle(0.7, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=1).set_stroke(INK, 4)
        ball = Circle(0.34, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1).set_stroke(INK, 3)
        axis = Line(DOWN*0.6, UP*0.6, color=WHITE, stroke_width=5).rotate(-23.4*DEGREES)
        earth = VGroup(ball, axis).move_to(orbit.point_from_proportion(0))
        label = MathTex(r'23.5^\circ', color=WHITE).scale(1.2).to_corner(UL)
        self.play(Create(orbit), FadeIn(sun), FadeIn(earth), Write(label), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(earth, orbit), run_time=7, rate_func=linear)

say: When your half of Earth leans toward the Sun, sunlight hits it more directly, and days are longer.

say: Six months later, your half leans away. The light is spread thin, and the days are short.
